_note: PLACEHOLDER STUDY CONTENT - standard-teaching level facts for the prototype, but every card needs a clinician's sign-off before this is shown to real users.

em.read: Anaphylaxis is treated first with IM adrenaline 500mcg into the anterolateral thigh, repeated every 5 minutes if needed, alongside high-flow oxygen and IV fluids.

em.q: target oxygen saturation with no risk of CO2 retention
em.read: For most acutely unwell patients without a risk of CO2 retention, oxygen therapy targets a saturation of 94 to 98 percent.

med.q: most common cause of community-acquired pneumonia
med.read: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains the most common organism isolated in community-acquired pneumonia across most age groups.

med.q: first-line rate control in stable atrial fibrillation
med.a: a beta-blocker or rate-limiting calcium channel blocker
med.read: Rate control in stable AF is usually achieved first with a beta-blocker or a rate-limiting calcium channel blocker such as diltiazem.

rad.a: a visible pleural line with no lung markings beyond it
rad.read: A pneumothorax on chest x-ray shows a thin visible pleural line, with no lung markings visible peripheral to that line.

rad.q: CT finding suggestive of acute appendicitis
rad.a: a dilated, non-compressible appendix over 6mm with fat stranding
rad.read: On CT, acute appendicitis typically shows a dilated, non-compressible appendix greater than 6mm in diameter with adjacent fat stranding.

path.q: cell type pathognomonic for Hodgkin lymphoma
path.read: Reed-Sternberg cells, large binucleate cells with prominent nucleoli, are considered pathognomonic for classical Hodgkin lymphoma.

path.q: most common subtype of renal cell carcinoma
path.read: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma is the most common subtype, accounting for the majority of renal cell carcinomas.

anaes.read: Normal end-tidal CO2 in a mechanically ventilated patient is roughly 35 to 45 mmHg, closely tracking arterial CO2 in most situations.

anaes.q: first drug given in a shockable adult cardiac arrest rhythm
anaes.a: adrenaline 1mg IV after the third shock
anaes.read: In a shockable rhythm during adult cardiac arrest, adrenaline 1mg IV is given after the third shock, then every other cycle.
